We have template info. The 'retro_smarts_template' is the retrosynthetic SMARTS (i.e., product->reactants). The 'mapped_rxn' is a reaction SMILES with mapping. We need to apply this template to the target molecule. The target molecule is likely the product side of the reaction. The mapped_rxn shows product on right side? Reaction SMILES format: reactants>>products. In mapped_rxn: '[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13]([CH:14]=[O:18])[O:21]1.C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1'

So left side (reactants) are two fragments: fragment A: [CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13]([CH:14]=[O:18])[O:21]1

fragment B: C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]

Product is the right side: a single molecule.

Thus the template is a retrosynthetic transformation that breaks product into two precursors (A and B). So applying the template to the product should give those two precursors.

Thus the precursors are exactly the left side fragments. We need to return them as SMILES strings (without mapping). We need to strip atom mapping numbers and maybe convert to SMILES.

We can extract the SMILES from the mapped_rxn left side fragments, removing atom map tags like :1 etc. The fragments:

Fragment A SMILES with mapping: [CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13]([CH:14]=[O:18])[O:21]1

Remove the :numbers: becomes CH3CH2O C(=O)CH2C@H1CH2C@H... need to convert to proper SMILES. Let's manually remove mapping: replace each atom with mapping like [CH3:1] -> CH3, [CH2:2] -> CH2, [O:3] -> O, [C:4] -> C, [O:5] -> O, [CH2:6] -> CH2, [C@H:7]1 -> C@H1, [CH2:8] -> CH2, [C@H:9] -> C@H, ([OH:10]) -> (OH), [C@@H:11] -> C@@H, ([CH3:12]) -> (CH3), [C@@H:13] -> C@@H, ([CH:14]=[O:18]) -> (C=O)?? Actually [CH:14]=[O:18] is CH=O? That's an aldehyde? So (C=O). Then [O:21]1 -> O1.

Thus fragment A SMILES: CH3CH2O C(=O)CH2C@H1CH2C@H(OH)C@@H(CH3)C@@H(C=O)O1

Combine: "CCO C(=O)C..." Let's write: "CCOC(=O)C1CC(O)C(C)C(C=O)O1"? Need to be careful.

Original fragment likely corresponds to the first SMILES from earlier: "O=CHCH2C1O[C@H](/C=C(C)CCH2OH)"? Not exactly. Let's maybe use the earlier precursors list: they gave two SMILES: "O=CHCH2C1O[C@H](/C=C(C)CCH2OH)" and "O=S(=O)(O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C(F)(F)F". That seems different.

Our fragment B: C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20] -> remove mapping: CCH(P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#C OCH3? Actually [C:15]#[C:17] is a carbon-carbon triple bond. [O:19][CH3:20] is OCH3. So fragment B is something like "C[C](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#COC"? Wait need to parse: C[CH:16](P(...))[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]. The first C is a methyl attached to CH (CH16). So it's "CC(P(...))C#COC". The triple bond carbon attached to OCH3.

Thus the precursors likely are those two fragments. We can output them as SMILES without mapping. Could we just output the left side fragments as given but with mapping removed? That should be acceptable.

Thus answer list: [["CCO..."], ["C..."]]. Let's construct approximate SMILES:

Fragment A: CH3CH2O C(=O) CH2 C@H1 CH2 C@H(OH) C@@H(CH3) C@@H(C=O) O1

Write as: "CCOC(=O)C1CC(O)C(C)C(C=O)O1". That seems plausible.

Fragment B: "CC(P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#COC". Actually OCH3 is OCH3, so "C#COC". So full: "CC(P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#COC". Need to include the methyl attached to the CH: "CC(P(...))C#COC". That is "CC(P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#COC". Might be correct.

Thus final answer list of list: [["CCOC(=O)C1CC(O)C(C)C(C=O)O1", "CC(P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)C#COC"]].

Return that.
